Zimbabwe Meltdown

By: Julian Sun | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We take you inside the repressive regime of Emmerson Mnangagwa's Zimbabwe

Unique Selling Point:
We take you inside Zimbabwe, a country experiencing a political and economic meltdown made worse but the COVID-19 pandemic. Inflation running rampant, citizens angry at government corruption, healthcare workers on strike, journalists arrested and a government desperate to cling onto power.

Summary:
We focus on the story of journalist Hopewell Chin’ono who has been in custody since July 31st. We have an interview with Beatirce Mtwetwe - human rights lawyer who was representing him until court in Zim barred her from doing so.

We have interviews with journalist Njabulo Ncube who will tell us about how journalists live in fear currently because they have been investigating and unearthing corruption and state capture by the Mnangagwa regime. Njabulo can also connect us with a spokesman from Zanu-PF if required

We also have an interview lined up with Zim political commentator Dr Ibbo Mandaza

The story will be shot by a Zimbabwean journalist/cameraman Farai Mugano. I want to get Masa to conduct the interviews via zoom/or Skype. We have a camera team in Zim and a Camera team in SA. Farai will be able to shoot extensive cutaways of life in Harare.

Here locally, I have engaged with former Deputy Public Protector Kevin Malunga (a Zimbabwean by origin) to give us insight into the state of the country.

Press Release:


Zimbabwe Teetering?
As Zimbabwean president Emmerson Mnangagwa offers compensation to farmers once affected by the land grabs that plunged the country into economic ruin, police step up their crackdown on dissent. Once dubbed ‘Africa’s breadbasket”, Zimbabwe is facing a long-standing political and economic crisis with little hope of a turnaround promised by the new president three years ago. Carte Blanche goes inside Zimbabwe where journalists and activists have been unlawfully imprisoned by his oppressive regime. With Zimbabweans suffering under the yolk of crippling inflation (as high as 800%) and severe shortages of everyday necessities, we ask how are ordinary people surviving?

Script:


SCRIPT
V/O: When Emmerson Mnangagwa swept to power on the back of a military coup back in 2017, a wave of hope and optimism swept Zimbabwe.

Sound up of President Mnangagwa

LINK: The promise by President Emmerson Mnangagwa of delivering the “Zimbabwe you want” has instead offered more of the same. HyperInflation, government corruption and a crackdown and arrest of journalists brave enough to reveal the truth.

So what’s gone wrong?

Kevin Malunga is the former Deputy Public Protector of South Africa. He’s a Zimbabwean who’s written extensively on the problems facing his country.

Kevin on President Mnangagwa’s broken promises

He must say the economy is in ruins, that people are hungry, there is food insecurity…

V/O: In a desperate bid to improve food security, the government struck a deal with former commercial farm owners, offering them compensation to the tune of 3.5 billion US$ for the land taken away from them, during the Robert Mugabe years.

Former farm owners can also apply to have the land returned to them. The deal is supposed to be financed through the sale of government bonds.

Kevin on the farm deal – it’s a sham

V/O: In recent months, discontent in Zimbabwe has been voiced by the likes of award-winning investigative journalist & activist Hopewell Chin’ono who went from being a Mnangawa admirer to one of his harshest critics.

In April he exposed a dodgy deal when a company affiliated with one the President’s sons won a tender worth $60 million to supply PPE.

Then in July he was arrested and detained at the notorious Chikurubi Prison until this week. Human Rights Lawyer Beatrice Mtetwa represented him

Beatrice tells the story of Hopewell’s arrest

V/O: It’s not just Hopewell who’s been targeted. The Mnangagwa regime has used the COVID-19 lockdown as cover to crackdown on any and all dissent, arresting opposition leaders and journalists. It has Njabulo Ncube fearful for himself and his colleagues.

Njabulo talks about how difficult it is for journalists to do their jobs in Zimbabwe

Njabulo on why the state is cracking down…

V/O: Beatrice Mtwetwa has also been persecuted by the Mnangagwa government.

She also describes her on persecution when a judge barred her from representing Hopewell



V/O: And while the government silences its critics, the people go hungry struggling under the weight of an inflation rate of over 800%

LINK 3: In a shop like this is in South Africa, we take for granted that the shelves fully stocked and you’d be able to afford the groceries you want. But can the same be said for the people of Zimbabwe

V/O: It’s a daily struggle for survival for most, including middle class citizens like Chancellor Muzenda.

He’s a systems engineer for a major bank, is studying for his MBA but struggles to support his family.

Chancellor tells us about life in Zimbabwe

Njabulo talks about a journalist salary of $50 and the cost of meat and bread

V/O: And while most struggle to make ends meet, Hopewell Chin’ono’s struggle goes on. This week it was reported that he was feeling ill with COVID-19 symptoms.

Beatrice on Hopewell’s illness

Then on Wednesday due to his illness, he was finally granted bail of $10 000 but under strict conditions.

Doug Coltart addresses media

V/O: So what does the future hold for the people of Zimbabwe?

The best Closing comment we can find.
